scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Nobody on? Throw to first.
scenarios.why: The only runner is the batter, and he is running to first base. Throw there.

scenarios.ask: Slow ground ball to you at first base. You are two steps from the bag.
scenarios.big: You're closer. Just step on it.
scenarios.why: You can beat the runner to the bag by yourself. No throw needed. Step on first.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right back to you on the mound.
scenarios.big: Bases loaded? Get the run at home.
scenarios.why: Every runner has to run, so the man on third has to go home. Throw to the catcher and stop the run.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base. You are two steps from the bag.
scenarios.big: He has to run. Step on second.
scenarios.why: The batter is running to first, so the runner has to leave first base. You are already there. Step on the bag.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at shortstop. The runner takes off for home.
scenarios.big: Two outs? Take the easy one.
scenarios.why: Let him run. If you get the batter at first for the third out, his run does not count.

scenarios.ask: Slow ground ball to you at third base. You have to run in and grab it.
scenarios.big: Slow ball? Take the sure out.
scenarios.why: The ball took too long to get to you. The runner is already at second. Throw to first.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at first base, right next to the bag.
scenarios.big: Nobody on first? He can stay put.
scenarios.why: The runner on second does not have to run. You can't force him out. Step on first and take the easy out.

scenarios.ask: Line drive! You catch it in the air at shortstop.
scenarios.big: You caught it. That's the out.
scenarios.why: The batter is out as soon as you catch it. There is nobody else to get. Give the ball back to the pitcher.

scenarios.ask: The ball dribbles in front of the plate. You grab it.
scenarios.big: Standing on the out? Take it.
scenarios.why: The runner on third has to run home. Home plate is right under your feet. Step on it.

scenarios.ask: Fly ball to center field. You catch it.
scenarios.big: After the catch, throw to second.
scenarios.why: He went halfway to watch the catch. Now he has to get back to first. Throw to second so he cannot change his mind and take it.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base.
scenarios.big: Playing back? Take the out.
scenarios.why: Your team is standing deep, so the run is going to score. That is okay. Get the out at first base.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base. You are three steps from the bag.
scenarios.big: Everybody has to run. Take the closest base.
scenarios.why: Both runners have to run, so any base is an out. Second base is closest. Step on it and the inning is over.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to your left. It pulls you toward first base.
scenarios.big: Go where the ball takes you.
scenarios.why: Second base is behind you now. First base is a force out too. Throw the way you are already moving.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right at you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Get two outs, not one.
scenarios.why: The runner on first has to run. Throw to second to start a double play. Two outs ends the inning.

scenarios.ask: Hard ground ball right at you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Two outs beats one run.
scenarios.why: Throwing home only gets one out. Second base can get two and end the inning.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right at you at third base.
scenarios.big: Look him back, then throw to first.
scenarios.why: He does not have to run, so you can't force him out. Stare at him for one second so he stops. Then throw to first.

scenarios.ask: Fly ball to right field. You catch it and the runner runs home.
scenarios.big: He's going home. Throw home.
scenarios.why: He waited for your catch, then took off. Throw to the catcher and try to beat him to the plate.

scenarios.ask: Fly ball to left field. You catch it.
scenarios.big: Count the outs first.
scenarios.why: There were already two outs. Your catch was the third one. The inning is over, so there is nobody to throw at.

scenarios.ask: Short fly ball to right field. You catch it. The runner is already near second.
scenarios.big: He left early. Throw behind him.
scenarios.why: He has to go back and touch first base. Throw to first before he gets there and he is out too.

scenarios.ask: The batter bunts it down the first base line. You grab it.
scenarios.big: Take the out they give you.
scenarios.why: The runner got a head start on the bunt. Don't chase him. Throw to first for the sure out.

scenarios.ask: The batter bunts up the third base line. You charge in and grab it.
scenarios.big: You left your base. Throw to first.
scenarios.why: You ran off third base to get the ball. The shortstop is running over to cover it. First base is the safe out.

scenarios.ask: The ball gets past you in left field. The runner rounds third and heads home.
scenarios.big: Long throw home? Keep it low.
scenarios.why: Throw low and hard toward the plate. Aim at the third baseman standing in the middle, so he can grab it if the throw is off.

scenarios.ask: The ball is hit to left field. You play right field. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Back up the base.
scenarios.why: Outfielders never stand still. Run in behind second base. If the throw gets past everybody, you are there to stop it.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to center. The throw is going home. You are the pitcher. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Pitchers back up the throw.
scenarios.why: Run behind the catcher and stand way back. If the throw gets past him, you stop it and nobody moves up.

scenarios.ask: Pop up over the mound. The umpire yells INFIELD FLY — the batter is out.
scenarios.big: Batter's already out. Just catch it.
scenarios.why: The umpire called him out so you can't drop it on purpose. Now nobody has to run. Catch the ball and hold it.

scenarios.ask: Deep fly ball to center. You catch it. The runner tags up and runs to third.
scenarios.big: He's only going one base. Throw to third.
scenarios.why: He is not going home, so home is the wrong throw. Throw toward third base. The shortstop runs out to help you.

scenarios.ask: The ball rolls into the corner in right field. You are very far from home plate.
scenarios.big: Too far? Hit your relay man.
scenarios.why: You can't throw that far on a line. The second baseman runs out to meet you. Throw to him and he throws the rest of the way.

scenarios.ask: Strike three! But the ball bounces off your glove and rolls away.
scenarios.big: Dropped strike three? He can run.
scenarios.why: If you drop strike three and first base is empty, the batter is allowed to run. Go get the ball and throw to first.

scenarios.ask: The ball pulls you way off of first base. The runner heads for third.
scenarios.big: The pitcher covers first.
scenarios.why: You are too far from the bag to get back in time. The pitcher runs over to cover first on every ball hit your way. Toss it to him, chest high. Forget the runner.

scenarios.ask: Hard ground ball to you at third. The runner on third takes off for home!
scenarios.big: He ran. Get him at the plate.
scenarios.why: He can't stop once he goes. You have the ball and he doesn't. Throw home and take the run away.

scenarios.ask: Hard ground ball to you at third base. The runner on third stays on the bag.
scenarios.big: Second base is empty, so third is not a force.
scenarios.why: Stepping on third does nothing — he does not have to run. The runner on first DOES have to run. Throw to second.

scenarios.ask: Hard ground ball to you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Playing in? Stop the run.
scenarios.why: Your team moved up close for one reason: to keep him from scoring. Throw home.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to right field. You play shortstop. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Somebody has to cover the bag.
scenarios.why: The second baseman ran out to the grass to take the relay throw. That leaves second base empty. You cover it.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to center field. He rounds third and sprints for home.
scenarios.big: Two outs? Let it rip.
scenarios.why: There is nothing to save the ball for. Throw hard toward the plate on one bounce.

scenarios.ask: Slow ground ball to your right at second base. You run in and grab it.
scenarios.big: Slow ball? Take the closest base.
scenarios.why: You might not beat the batter to first. Everybody has to run, so second base is an out too — and it is much closer.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at third base.
scenarios.big: Only one runner. Get him at first.
scenarios.why: The batter is the only runner, and he is running to first base. Throw across and beat him there.

scenarios.ask: The ball comes right back to you on the mound.
scenarios.big: Easy out. Toss it to first.
scenarios.why: The batter is the only runner. Take your time, turn, and make a good throw to first base.

scenarios.ask: The ball dribbles out in front of the plate. You grab it.
scenarios.big: Grab it and fire to first.
scenarios.why: The batter took off for first base as soon as he hit it. He is the only runner. Throw him out.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to you in left field. The batter is running to first.
scenarios.big: Throw it in ahead of him.
scenarios.why: He already has first base. Second base is where he wants to go next. Throw to second so he stops at first.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Get the lead runner at second.
scenarios.why: The runner from first is heading to second. He is the lead runner. Throw to second before he gets there.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at first base, but you are far off the bag.
scenarios.big: Off the bag? Get the lead runner.
scenarios.why: You are too far from first to race the batter there. The lead runner is heading to second. Throw ahead of him.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to you in center field. The lead runner is rounding second.
scenarios.big: He wants third. Beat him there.
scenarios.why: The lead runner is already past second base. Third base is where he is going. Throw to third and make him stop.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Two runners on? The lead one wants third.
scenarios.why: The runner from second is the lead runner now, and he is heading to third base. Throw ahead of HIM, not the one behind.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right at you at third base.
scenarios.big: The lead runner is coming to YOU.
scenarios.why: The runner from second is heading right to your base. You do not even need to throw. Step on third and he is out.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base.
scenarios.big: The force is right next to you.
scenarios.why: The runner from first has to run to second, and you are standing right by the bag. Take the easy force out.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to you in right field. The lead runner is heading for third.
scenarios.big: Throw to third and stop him.
scenarios.why: The lead runner is trying to take third base. Get the ball there first and he has to stop.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to you in left field. The lead runner is rounding third.
scenarios.big: Now home is the base ahead of him.
scenarios.why: The lead runner is past third and running for the plate. Home is the base ahead of him now. Throw it home.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Loaded up? The out is next to you.
scenarios.why: With the bases loaded, every runner has to run. Second base is just a few steps away. The short flip beats the long throw home.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at third base.
scenarios.big: Home is one throw away. Take it.
scenarios.why: The runner from third is the lead runner and he is almost home. You are close. Make the short throw to the plate.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base.
scenarios.big: Take the sure out at your bag.
scenarios.why: Every base has a runner, so second is a force — and it is right there. The easy out now beats a long throw home that might get away.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to the shortstop. You are the pitcher. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Every throw needs a backup.
scenarios.why: The throw is going to first base. Run behind first, way back. If the throw gets away, you are there to save it.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to third. The throw is going to first. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Back up the throw at first.
scenarios.why: Right field is behind first base. Run in toward the line. If the throw gets past first, you are the one who saves it.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to the shortstop. You play center field. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: No ball? You still have a job.
scenarios.why: The shortstop will throw to second base. Run in behind second. If the ball gets past, you are there to stop it.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to the third baseman. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: His throw needs a place to land.
scenarios.why: The third baseman is going to throw to first base. That is YOUR base. Get to the bag and be ready to catch it.

scenarios.ask: The shortstop calls the ground ball. Where do YOU go?
scenarios.big: Don't chase it. Cover your base.
scenarios.why: Only one player fields the ball, and this time it is not you. Your job is third base. Go stand on your bag.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right at you at third base. The runner stays on second.
scenarios.big: He can stay there. Go get the batter.
scenarios.why: Nobody is behind him, so he does not have to run. Stepping on third does nothing. Take the sure out at first.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right at you at third base.
scenarios.big: Now he HAS to run. The bag is the out.
scenarios.why: There is a runner behind him now, so the man on second has to run to third. You are standing on his base. Step on it.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at shortstop. The runner takes off for third, right past you.
scenarios.big: No force? You have to tag HIM.
scenarios.why: He ran right into you — tag him. If he had gone by out of your reach, the play would be the sure out at first instead.

labels.tagrunner: Tag him as he goes by

scenarios.ask: Ground ball deep in the hole, far to your right. The runner takes off for third.
scenarios.big: Out of reach? Take the sure out.
scenarios.why: He is too far away to tag, and no throw beats him to third from out there. The batter is the out you can still get. First base.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base.
scenarios.big: Third out ends it. Run can't count.
scenarios.why: Step on second for the force. The inning is over before the runner from third can score, so his run does not count.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base. The runner on third breaks for home.
scenarios.big: Both work. Ask your coach.
scenarios.why: Stepping on second is the sure out, but the run scores. Throwing home can stop the run, but it is a long throw. Ask your coach which one he wants.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at first base, right next to the bag.
scenarios.big: They can stay. The batter can't.
scenarios.why: The runners on second and third do not have to move. The only sure out is the batter, and your bag is waiting. Step on first.

scenarios.ask: The ball drops right at your feet. The runner from third breaks for home.
scenarios.big: Nobody behind him? You have to tag him.
scenarios.why: Stepping on the plate does nothing here. Nobody is behind him, so he does not have to run. You have to tag the runner.

scenarios.ask: The ball drops right at your feet. The runner from third breaks for home.
scenarios.big: Bases loaded? The plate is enough.
scenarios.why: Every base is full, so he HAS to run home. That makes it a force. Step on the plate — no tag needed this time.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right at you at third base. Both runners stay put.
scenarios.big: Two on, and NOBODY has to run.
scenarios.why: There is no runner on first, so nothing pushes them. They can both stay. The only out you can force is the batter at first.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball deep in the hole. It takes you far to your right.
scenarios.big: Two outs? The closest force ends it.
scenarios.why: Third base is a long throw from way out there. Second base is closer, and any force ends the inning with two outs. Take the short one.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at first base. The runner on third takes off for home.
scenarios.big: Let him go. The bag ends it.
scenarios.why: With two outs, the force at first ends the inning. If you step on the bag before the batter gets there, his run never counts.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to you in center. The lead runner is around second and not stopping.
scenarios.big: He's not stopping. Make him.
scenarios.why: The lead runner is trying to steal an extra base on you. One hop to third base cuts him down or sends him back.

scenarios.ask: Fly ball to you in left field. You catch it, and the runner is way off second.
scenarios.big: He forgot to go back. Make him pay.
scenarios.why: After a catch, the runner has to touch his base again. He is too far away. Throw to second before he can get back.

scenarios.ask: The ball rolls into the gap. The runner from first is heading for third.
scenarios.big: Too far to throw? Find your relay.
scenarios.why: The shortstop is running out to help you. Hit him with your throw, and he will fire it to third. Two short throws beat one long one.

scenarios.ask: The ball rolls all the way to the fence. The runner from second is heading home.
scenarios.big: From the fence, you need help.
scenarios.why: Nobody can throw home from the fence. The shortstop is waiting in the middle for your throw. Get it to him fast and low.

scenarios.ask: Base hit gets past you in right field. The runner from first is digging for third.
scenarios.big: Your relay man is already moving.
scenarios.why: The second baseman is running out to meet you. Throw it to him hard, and he will send it on to third. That is his job on every ball to right.

scenarios.ask: The batter bunts it up the line. You charge in and grab it.
scenarios.big: You made the play. Take the out.
scenarios.why: The bunt did its job — the runner is already near second. Do not chase him. First base is the out you can still get.

scenarios.ask: The batter bunts down the line. You charge off the bag to field it.
scenarios.big: The 2nd baseman has your bag.
scenarios.why: You left first base to get the ball, but you are not alone. The second baseman runs over to cover first. Flip it to him.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to left field. The throw is going to third. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: No one behind third? That's you.
scenarios.why: The throw from left field is coming to third base. Run over behind the bag and stand deep. If it skips through, you save a run.

scenarios.ask: The runner takes off to steal second. The shortstop yells that he has the bag. Where do YOU go?
scenarios.big: He covers. You back him up.
scenarios.why: Two players on one bag helps nobody. Your job is behind the bag, in line with the throw. If it gets past him, you are there.

scenarios.ask: The runner takes off to steal second. It is your bag to cover. Where do YOU go?
scenarios.big: You called it. Get to the bag.
scenarios.why: Beat the runner to second and give the catcher a target. Catch the throw in front of the bag and put the tag down.

scenarios.ask: The runner steals second and the catcher lets it fly. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Every steal needs a safety net.
scenarios.why: If the throw gets past the infield, that runner is taking third. Charge in behind second base and be the wall.

scenarios.ask: Pop up right to you. The umpire yells INFIELD FLY — the batter is out.
scenarios.big: The call already made the out.
scenarios.why: The umpire's call means the batter is out no matter what. The runners can stay put. Catch it, hold it, and relax.

scenarios.ask: Pop up straight over your head. The umpire yells INFIELD FLY.
scenarios.big: Your easiest out. Don't rush it.
scenarios.why: The batter is already out on the call, and nobody has to run. Camp under it, make the catch, and keep the ball.

scenarios.ask: The ball dribbles out in front of the plate. The runner breaks for home.
scenarios.big: The count says take the batter.
scenarios.why: Chasing him is a race you might lose. With two outs, the out at first ends the inning, and then his run counts for nothing.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to you in right field. The runner is around third and heading home.
scenarios.big: Two outs? Send it all the way.
scenarios.why: This run is the whole play — with two outs there is no double play to set up. Skip the cutoff man and let it fly home on one hop.

scenarios.ask: The ball comes right back to you on the mound. The runner on third is not moving.
scenarios.big: He froze? Take what he gave you.
scenarios.why: Look him back to third so he stays put. Then turn and get the sure out at first. He decided this play for you when he froze.

scenarios.ask: Deep fly ball to you in left. You catch it, and he tags up for third.
scenarios.big: Throw to where he's GOING.
scenarios.why: The catch is out one — now he is trying to take third. Second base is behind him and does not matter. One hop to third base.

scenarios.ask: The ball splits the gap. The runner is around second and going for third.
scenarios.big: Hit the cutoff, hard and low.
scenarios.why: From the gap, third base is too far to reach on a line. The shortstop is your cutoff — hit him chest high and let him finish it.

scenarios.ask: The ball bangs off the wall. The runner from second is coming all the way around.
scenarios.big: The wall means you need two throws.
scenarios.why: No one scores a runner from the wall with one throw. Find the shortstop lined up in the middle. Your job is a hard strike to him, not a hero throw home.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right to you at third base.
scenarios.big: Feed second and turn two.
scenarios.why: The runner from first has to run, so second base starts the double play. One out is fine. Two outs for one ground ball is better.

scenarios.ask: The bunt rolls up the third base line. The third baseman charges it. Where do YOU go?
scenarios.big: He left third. Fill it.
scenarios.why: When the third baseman charges, his bag is empty behind him — and a runner is headed there. Whoever is free has to fill it. That is you.

scenarios.ask: The bunt dies right in front of the mound. You field it clean.
scenarios.big: Clean or not, first is certain.
scenarios.why: Third base is tempting, but that throw has to beat a runner with a head start. First base cannot be beaten. Take the certain out.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right to you at first base.
scenarios.big: You moved up for THIS throw.
scenarios.why: The whole infield stepped in to cut this run down at the plate. That was the deal. Fire it home and make the plan work.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to left. The throw is going home — and the batter is watching it. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: The throw home opens second base.
scenarios.why: When the throw goes home, the batter will try to sneak into second. Get behind the bag. If nobody covers the sneak, the hit turns into a double.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to right field. The throw is going to third. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Chase the throw, not the ball.
scenarios.why: Your job after the pitch is to back up the base the throw is going to. That is third this time. Get deep behind the bag.

scenarios.ask: INFIELD FLY is called — and the ball pops out of your glove. The runner from second takes off for third.
scenarios.big: The drop changes nothing. Tag him.
scenarios.why: The batter was out the moment the umpire called it, drop or no drop. Nobody HAS to run, so there is no force. The bag means nothing — tag the runner.

labels.tagrunner: Tag him as he goes by

scenarios.ask: INFIELD FLY is called. The ball drops in front of you, and both runners stay put.
scenarios.big: Dropped or caught, it's over.
scenarios.why: The call already made the batter out. The runners are smart to stay. Pick it up, hold it, and let the play die.

scenarios.ask: Strike three bounces off your glove — but first base is taken, and there is one out.
scenarios.big: First is taken. He can't run.
scenarios.why: Strike three can only run when first base is open or there are two outs. Not now. He is out on the call — hold the ball and relax.

scenarios.ask: Strike three skips past the catcher, and the batter takes off. Where do YOU go?
scenarios.big: The catcher needs a target. You.
scenarios.why: With two outs, strike three can always run. The catcher will grab it and fire — someone has to be standing on first. Go be there.

scenarios.ask: The ball comes right back to you, hard.
scenarios.big: From here, home is a gift. Take it.
scenarios.why: A shortstop would start two from deep. You are five feet from a certain out at home. Where you stand picks the play — toss it to the catcher.
